title: T-26, two players: the host's OWN logistics plan uses the CLIENT's warehouse - its add-shop limit is the client's per-slot total plus the host manager's skill bonus, a shop can be added, and the hourly pass delivers: the client (who runs the warehouse) withdraws, the host delivers to its shop, the client closes it out; a resend (the same pass AND the hand-over sent again) moves nothing twice; an EXPORT leg from the client's warehouse is withdrawn there and paid once on the host; ends dissolved WITHOUT a save
preconditions: Fixture save1 (the host melaus owns a warehouse logistics plan with a manager - its destinations may already fill the limit (dests=8=limit seen in run 20261113-033632), so the run frees ONE slot through the game's own remove (`lmcap drop last`) and puts that very destination back at its index (`lmcap undrop`), asserting the count returns to its before-value; the host's world holds at least one import/export business registration (lmexport's destination - Inferred, not verified on the fixture); Client1 owns a warehouse with a truck AND a driver in at least one slot (its stock is put in by whstock); the host's first own non-warehouse business in registration order has a sale shelf set to some item). Build with the T-26 levers lmsource / lmcap (incl. next, drop, undrop) / lmpass / whstock / stockof ... since / cargoresend / lmexport. The fixture has no known partner FACTORY plan with stock, so the export hand-over is driven by the lever-level check lmexport (an own plan briefly marked a factory plan for one TakeOver call). FIXTURE HYGIENE: lmsource, lmcap add and lmcap drop change one plan in memory and are undone before the dissolve (lmexport never puts its destination on the plan); the export pays the company wallet in memory only; the run never saves, so the fixture .hsg files are untouched (the manifest is reset before every run).
